scenes.tts: A lumber merchant's son once written off as too dull for business, Fischer became the most exacting organic chemist in Germany by reading structure off behavior.
scenes.visual: lumber merchant's son to exacting chemist; structure off behavior
scenes.narration: A lumber merchant's son once written off as too dull for business, Fischer became the most exacting organic chemist in Germany by reading structure off behavior.

scenes.tts: Through the 1880s and 1890s he wrestled the sugars into order using osazones, oxidation, and the cyanohydrin chain-extension, deducing which hydroxyl pointed which way long before any instrument could see a molecule.
scenes.visual: 1880s-1890s; osazones, oxidation, cyanohydrin; hydroxyl direction; no instrument
scenes.narration: Through the 1880s and 1890s he wrestled the sugars into order using osazones, oxidation, and the cyanohydrin chain-extension, deducing which hydroxyl pointed which way long before any instrument could see a molecule.

scenes.tts: The Fischer projection you will draw in this chapter is the notation he invented to keep that three-dimensional bookkeeping straight on flat paper, and the D/L convention is his.
scenes.visual: Fischer projection: 3D bookkeeping on flat paper; D/L
scenes.narration: The Fischer projection you will draw in this chapter is the notation he invented to keep that three-dimensional bookkeeping straight on flat paper, and the D/L convention is his.

scenes.tts: From the same work came his "lock and key" image of enzyme specificity — the idea that a protein and its sugar must fit together geometrically — which is exactly the principle the lectins at the end of this lesson run on.
scenes.visual: lock and key: protein and sugar fit; lectins

scenes.tts: The phenylhydrazine that let him fingerprint the sugars also, slowly, poisoned him; he died in 1919.
